start.text: Welcome, {name}. The waystone remembers travellers who rest beside it.

saved.text: Done. If you faint or use a Butterfly Wing, you'll wake up right here.

rested.text: You feel refreshed. HP and SP fully restored.

start.text: Tonics, wings and fresh apples! Got loot to sell? I'll pay half what it's worth, which is more than the monsters will.

wings.text: A Fly Wing whisks you to a random spot on the same map. A Butterfly Wing takes you straight home to your return point. Green Herbs cure poison, and a Panacea cures anything.

fight.text: Tap a monster and you'll walk up and keep attacking. Sit to recover faster, and keep a few Red Tonics on hand.

where.text: Take the road south to the Southern Meadow. The Jellops there are harmless unless you poke them.

stronger.text: Every level gives stat points: open Stats to spend them. At job level 5 you can join a guild: Swordsmen (Captain Harlan), Mages (Magister Ilse), Archers (Wren) or Acolytes (Sister Maren). Sell loot to Bram so your bag never gets too heavy.

menu.text: New in Brightmoor? I'm Pell. Ask me anything.

splinter.text: He sees it before you say anything. “Put that away.” A pause. “Don’t show Nim.”

again.text: “I said put it away.” He doesn’t look at you for the rest of the day.

ep_gap.text: He stops, as if you’d spoken. “…You’re warm. You weren’t, a moment ago.”

start.text: Swordsman Guild. You look like you could swing a blade, {name}.

choices.label: I want to become a Swordsman

not_ready.text: Not yet. Reach job level 5 and put 4 skill points into Basic Training. Open Skills to spend them.

fee.text: You've trained well. Your trial: bring me 10 Jelly Drops from the Southern Meadow. A Swordsman finishes what they start.

ready.text: 10 Jelly Drops, and the scars to prove it. Hand them over and swear the Swordsman's oath?

welcome.text: Welcome to the Guild, Swordsman {name}! You keep your unspent skill points. Open Skills and learn Bash first.

about.text: Swordsmen take hits and hit back harder. You'll learn Bash for heavy single blows, Magnum Break to blast a crowd, and Endure to shrug off damage.

shards1.text: “Whatever that golem guarded, it guarded well. Don’t undo its work.”

shards2.text: “A king tried to wear it. Remember how that ended.”

shards3.text: “Some doors are meant to stay closed.”

start.text: Greta's forge. Blades, shields, boots: if it keeps you alive out there, I make it.

howto.text: Open Items and tap Equip next to a piece of gear. The Gear tab shows what you're wearing. Some pieces are for Swordsmen only, and some need a higher level.

refine_info.text: Each attempt costs one Brightstone and some gold. Up to +4 I never fail. Past that, the metal can resist me: then the ore and gold are spent, but your gear comes back exactly as it was. I'll show you the odds first.

start.text: The Circle of Mages. Magic is patience, {name}, and a good deal of standing still.

choices.label: I want to become a Mage

not_ready.text: Not yet. Reach job level 5 and put 4 skill points into Basic Training.

fee.text: Your trial: bring me 5 Beetle Shells from Thornfield, east of the Southern Meadow. Their shells focus mana. Mind the beetles: they bite first.

ready.text: Five shells, still warm. Hand them over and take the Circle's vow?

welcome.text: Welcome to the Circle, Mage {name}! Learn a bolt in Skills. Casting takes time and a hit will break your focus, so strike from afar. Greta sells staves.

about.text: Mages hurl Fire, Cold and Lightning Bolts from nine tiles away and pick the element a monster is weak to. Soul Strike hits anything. Raise INT for power and DEX to cast faster.

shards1.text: “Feel how it pulls? That isn’t magic. That’s appetite.”

shards2.text: “The old empire ran on it. Ran out, too.”

shards3.text: “Every engine needs a heart. Ask whose.”

start.text: HUNTING BOARD. Hunts posted by the town: take up to three at a time, each pays once. Every monster you defeat also earns a standing bounty, paid out here.

choices.label: Read the hunts and collect bounty

start.text: Archer's Lodge. You walk loud, {name}. Out in the woods, that gets you eaten.

choices.label: I want to become an Archer

not_ready.text: Not yet. Reach job level 5 and put 4 skill points into Basic Training.

fee.text: Your trial: bring me 6 Moss Clumps from Mossy Hollow, south of Thornfield. Mosslings hide in plain sight. Learn to spot them.

ready.text: Six clumps, nice and damp. Hand them over and take the Lodge's oath?

welcome.text: Welcome to the Lodge, Archer {name}! Greta sells bows. With one equipped you shoot from five tiles away, so let them come to you. Learn Double Strafe in Skills.

about.text: Archers shoot from afar with a bow. Double Strafe fires two arrows at once, Arrow Shower hits a whole pack, and Owl's Eye sharpens your aim. Raise DEX for damage and AGI for speed.

shards1.text: “The wolves went quiet the night you found it.”

start.text: Welcome to the chapel, {name}. Everyone who walks in is tired. Sit a while.

choices.label: I want to become an Acolyte

not_ready.text: Not yet. Reach job level 5 and put 4 skill points into Basic Training.

fee.text: Your trial is a kindness: bring 4 Sweet Apples for the children of the chapel. Bram sells them, or the meadow provides.

ready.text: Four apples. The children will be delighted. Take the chapel's blessing?

welcome.text: Welcome, Acolyte {name}. Learn Heal in Skills and you'll never need a tonic again. Blessing and Increase AGI make you stronger and faster. Greta sells maces.

about.text: Acolytes heal themselves, bless their body and mind, and burn the undead with Holy Light. Raise INT for stronger heals and more SP.

shards1.text: “I prayed over it. Something prayed back.”

start.text: Fresh off the boats! Blue Tonics for the spell-slingers, boots for the deckhands. Have a look.
Hello, {name}! Lonely out there? A little friend makes every road shorter.

choices.label: How do I tame a pet?
How do I care for it?

how.text: Buy the lure for the monster you want, walk within 6 tiles of one and use the lure from your bag. Wear it down a bit first: a tired monster is much easier to win over.

care.text: Tap your pet to open its window. Feed it a Pet Treat when it's hungry and it grows fond of you. Once it trusts you it helps: stronger stats, and Jellops and Gullwings pick up loot for you. Starve it and it will leave.

start.text: The Order of the Sun Shield. We guard the caravans and the weak, {name}.

choices.label: I want to become a Knight

not_ready.text: You have promise, but not yet. Come back at job level 25 as a Swordsman.

fee.text: Your trial: bring me 10 Scorpion Tails from the Sunscorch Dunes. Stand your ground when they swarm.

ready.text: Ten tails. You held the line. Kneel, and rise a Knight?

welcome.text: Rise, Sir {name}! Learn Pierce and Bowling Bash in Skills. A Claymore and Two-Hand Quicken make you a storm of steel, and Riding gets you there faster. Zahra sells Claymores.

about.text: Knights are the front line. Pierce hits big monsters several times, Bowling Bash knocks a whole pack around, Two-Hand Quicken speeds up two-handed swords, and Riding makes you faster on your feet.

shards1.text: “Whatever that golem guarded, it guarded well. Don’t undo its work.”

shards2.text: “A king tried to wear it. Remember how that ended.”

shards3.text: “Some doors are meant to stay closed.”

start.text: The Tower of Embers. Few climb it, {name}; fewer come down unchanged.

choices.label: I want to become a Wizard

not_ready.text: You have promise, but not yet. Come back at job level 25 as a Mage.

fee.text: Your trial: three Sand Rubies. Scorpions and Sandworms swallow them; take them back.

ready.text: Three rubies, burning with sunlight. Hand them over and take the Wizard's mark?

welcome.text: Welcome, Wizard {name}. Sight Rasher clears what surrounds you, Thunderstorm and Meteor Storm rain on whole packs. Long casts: keep your distance. Zahra sells the Arc Wand.

about.text: Wizards trade speed for power. Their area spells hit everything near the target, but the casts are long and a single hit breaks them. DEX shortens them.

shards1.text: “Feel how it pulls? That isn’t magic. That’s appetite.”

shards2.text: “The old empire ran on it. Ran out, too.”

shards3.text: “Every engine needs a heart. Ask whose.”

start.text: Ranger's Lodge. The desert hides everything, {name}. A good hunter finds it anyway.

choices.label: I want to become a Hunter

not_ready.text: You have promise, but not yet. Come back at job level 25 as a Archer.

fee.text: Your trial: 10 Sand Pelts from the Sand Wolves of the dunes. They blend into the sand, so look closely.

ready.text: Ten pelts, clean cuts. Ready to take the falcon?

welcome.text: Welcome, Hunter {name}! Your falcon strikes with Blitz Beat (DEX and INT make it hit harder), and Claymore Trap blasts a pack. Zahra sells Hunter Bows.

about.text: Hunters fight beside a falcon. Blitz Beat never misses, Steel Crow sharpens its talons, and Claymore Trap blows up anything next to your target.

shards1.text: “The wolves went quiet the night you found it.”

start.text: Temple of the Sun. Even here, {name}, the dead do not always rest.

choices.label: I want to become a Priest

not_ready.text: You have promise, but not yet. Come back at job level 25 as a Acolyte.

fee.text: Your trial: bring 10 Old Bones from the Sunken Ruins so we can lay them to rest. Holy Light will serve you there.

ready.text: Ten bones, finally at peace. Take the Priest's vows?

welcome.text: Welcome, Priest {name}. Kyrie Eleison shields you, Impositio Manus strengthens your arm, and Magnus Exorcismus purges the undead. Zahra sells the Holy Scepter.

about.text: Priests shield and purge. Kyrie Eleison absorbs blows, Impositio Manus adds attack, and Magnus Exorcismus smites every undead and shadow monster in an area.

shards1.text: “I prayed over it. Something prayed back.”

start.text: Sunspire Bazaar! Steel for Knights, wands for Wizards, bows, scepters and everything for the road.
Dax, first mate of the Gull. We sail back to Saltmere whenever you like.
Captain Rook. My ship sails south to the desert city of Sunspire. The crossing's rough and the sands are rougher: it's no place for anyone under level 30.

desert.text: Scorpions the size of carts, wolves you can't see against the sand, and the Sunken Ruins, where the Dust Pharaoh still holds court. The guilds of Sunspire train Knights, Wizards, Hunters and Priests.

cargo.text: “Same stones, every crossing. Someone in the sand pays double.” He watches the water. “Your friend sailed with me last month. Paid in glass. Didn’t come back.”

start.text: Courier Guild, at your service, {name}! We keep your things safe and get you where you're going.

warp.text: Where to? Travel between towns is free, but only to towns you've already been.

saved.text: Done! If you faint, or use a Butterfly Wing, you'll come back here.

about.text: One storage, shared by all of your adventurers. Store anything here and any of them can take it out at any Courier Guild office. It holds 100 different things.

howto.text: Bring me what monsters drop and a little gold, and I'll turn it into tonics, wings or gear. Shells, pelts and shards for the basics; gear cogs, power cells and scrap from the Iron Wastes for the good stuff. The bench shows what you're short of.

menu.text: Nim's Tinkery! Scrap in, wonders out. Got anything that clanks?

splinter.text: Nim stops working. “That’s— where did you find that?” A long look. “Leave it with me. I won’t ask twice.”

left.text: Nim wraps it in cloth without touching it. “Thank you.” It doesn’t sound like thanks.

kept.text: “Your choice.” Nim goes back to work, and doesn’t look up again.

hums.text: “It hums at night. I don’t sleep much.” Nim rubs tired eyes. “Anyway. Scrap in, wonders out.”

dark.text: “The cells went dark. All of them, the same night.” Nim turns one over in the light. “Scrap in. Scrap out.”

start.text: Vale's workshop. The desert eats machines, so I rebuild them. What do you need?

howto.text: Bring me what monsters drop and a little gold, and I'll turn it into tonics, wings or gear. Shells, pelts and shards for the basics; gear cogs, power cells and scrap from the Iron Wastes for the good stuff. The bench shows what you're short of.

start.text: A tinker's workbench, free for anyone to use. Bring what monsters drop and a little gold.
Short on something for the crafting table? Anything you've brought back from the wild, I keep in stock. Full price, mind.

ring.text: The trees here lean away from the middle. The ground there is warm.

buried.text: The ground takes it. The trees straighten, a little.

after.text: The trees stand straight here now. The ground is cold.

map.text: Pell’s desk. Everything is gone but a map: Sunspire, circled twice. Something east of it, scratched out.

empty.text: An empty desk. He left in a hurry, or wanted it to look that way.

gone.text: The desk is bare. Nobody has asked about him. Nobody seems to remember he was here.

one.text: An old man among the stones, writing in the dust with one finger. “We gave it a name. That was the mistake.”

two.text: “It answers to nothing now. Not even you.”

three.text: He doesn’t look up. “Don’t name it. Whatever you do.”

who.text: “I kept the records. Then I kept them from being read.” He wipes the dust clean.

start.text: The throne is cold. The crown on it is cracked, and too small for the skull beneath it.

left.text: You leave it where he left it.

one.text: Scrap, stacked with care. Someone took their time.

three.text: It’s facing the Citadel. It wasn’t, before.

start.text: Pell, among the machines. They work around him and don’t touch him. “You found the map.” A breath. “Of course you did.”

why.text: “It isn’t a weapon. It’s a door. Someone has to stand in it.”

fought.text: He doesn’t raise his sword. Then he’s gone.

start.text: “Go on. I’ll be here either way.”

hn_swordsman.text: Three fragments fit together. In the middle, a gap the size of a splinter. Your oathstone is heavy in your pocket. Some doors are meant to stay closed.

choices.label: Set the splinter in the gap

end_silence.text: The light goes out of them. Out of everything, a little.

end_crown.text: They answer to you now. So does everything that comes for them.

end_return.text: It rises. The roof was never meant to hold it. Far above, a star goes out, and one comes back.

end_gap.text: Pell was right. It’s a door. You are what stands in it.
